rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is a drink poured down from above into the chambers and homes of the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: شرب ينصب عليهم من علو في غرفهم ومنازلهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: An alternative says Tasnim flows through the air and descends into the vessels of Paradise's people, stopping when each vessel is full; Baghawī identifies this as Qatāda's view.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from height: an elevated thing is called a sanām, as in a camel's hump.
rows.anchor: للشيء المرتفع: سنام، ومنه: سنام البعير.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes Tasnim as the noblest drink.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: هو شرار اسمه تسنيم، وهو أشرف الشراب.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās say the brought-near drink Tasnim undiluted, while it is mixed into the drink of the other people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وابن عباس: هو خالص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked what “from Tasnim” means, Ibn ʿAbbās connects it with the hidden delights described in 32:17.
rows.anchor: وروى يوسف بن مهران عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه سئل عن قوله: "من تسنيم"؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAynan is parsed as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).
rows.anchor: {عينا} نصب على الحال {يشرب بها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase yashrabu bihā means that the brought-near drink from the spring.
rows.anchor: يشرب بها} أي منها وقيل:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss says the brought-near drink it undiluted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يشرب بها المقربون صرفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners are the polytheist Quraysh, including Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and their wealthy Meccan associates.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار قريش: أبا جهل، والوليد بن المغيرة، والعاص بن وائل، وأصحابهم من مترفي مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and their poor Muslim companions, whom the sinners mocked.
rows.anchor: عمار، وخباب، وصهيب، وبلال، وأصحابهم من فقراء المؤمنين. {يضحكون} وبهم يستهزؤن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The splitting of the sky is one of the signs of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: انشقاقها من علامات القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky hears its Lord's command to split and obeys; the wording is associated with hearing by the ear.
rows.anchor: وأطاعته، من الأذن وهو الاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is right and fitting for the sky to obey its Lord.
rows.anchor: وحق لها أن تطيع ربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is stretched like a leather hide from the ʿUkāẓ market and enlarged.
rows.anchor: مد الأديم العكاظي، وزيد في سعتها.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqātil says the earth is smoothed like a hide, leaving no building or mountain.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: سويت كمد الأديم، فلا يبقى فيها بناء ولا جبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth casts out its dead and treasures and is emptied of them.
rows.anchor: أخرجت {ما فيها} من الموتى والكنوز

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the apodosis of idhā as omitted: when these events occur, people will see reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في جواب "إذا" قيل: جوابه محذوف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes verse 84:6 the apodosis: when the sky splits, each striver meets what he has done.
rows.anchor: وقيل جوابه: "يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح"

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view makes “and it heard” the apodosis and treats the conjunction wāw as additional.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جوابه: "وأذنت" وحينئذ تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadḥ is a person's striving and effort in good or evil until it leaves an effect on him; the human is striving toward his Lord through his deeds.
rows.anchor: أي ساع إليه في عملك، والكدح: عمل الإنسان

rows.speaker: قتادة والكلبي والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Kalbī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain it as doing deeds for one's Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والكلبي والضحاك: عامل لربك عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone meets the recompense of their deeds, whether good or evil.
rows.anchor: أي ملاقي جزاء عملك خيرا كان أو شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to a person is the register of their deeds.
rows.anchor: {فأما من أوتي كتابه} ديوان [أعماله] (1) {بيمينه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha asks how easy reckoning fits the statement that whoever is reckoned is punished; the Prophet explains that easy reckoning is only presentation, while close questioning destroys a person. Baghawī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قالت: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من حوسب عذب" قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها فقلت: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person returns to his family in Paradise, including the houris and human women, joyful at the good and honor he has received.
rows.anchor: يعني في الجنة من الحور العين والآدميات {مسرورا}

words: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His right hand is shackled to his neck, his left hand placed behind his back, and his book given to him in that left hand from behind.
rows.anchor: فتغل يده اليمنى إلى عنقه وتجعل يده الشمال وراء ظهره، فيؤتى كتابه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the person's left hand is dislocated and brought from behind his back.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تخلع يده اليسرى من وراء ظهره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On reading his book he cries out for woe and destruction, saying “woe to me”; Baghawī links this to 25:13.
rows.anchor: ينادي بالويل والهلاك إذا قرأ كتابه يقول: يا ويلاه يا ثبوراه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل البصرة وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, the Basrans, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read yuṣlā with fatḥa on yāʾ and a light lām, as in 87:12.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، وأهل البصرة، وعاصم، وحمزة: و"يصلى" بفتح الياء خفيفا

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers use the passive yuṣallā, with ḍamma on yāʾ and a doubled lām; Baghawī compares 56:94 and 69:31.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بضم الياء [وفتح الصاد] (1) وتشديد اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asking why they do not believe is a rebuke in the form of an interrogative.
rows.anchor: {فما لهم لا يؤمنون} استفهام إنكار.

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil gloss their failure to prostrate as failure to pray.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: لا يصلون.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Companions prostrated with the Prophet during recitation of al-ʿAlaq and al-Inshiqāq; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سجدنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says he prayed the night prayer behind Abū Hurayra, who prostrated after reciting al-Inshiqāq and said he had prostrated behind the Prophet and would continue doing so until they met.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: صليت مع أبي هريرة العتمة فقرأ إذا السماء انشقت، فسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should look thoughtfully at what kind of thing his Lord created him from.
rows.anchor: أي من أي شيء خلقه ربه، أي فلينظر نظر المتفكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dāfiq water is semen poured into the womb; dāfiq means poured, though its active form carries a passive sense, as in “a pleasing life,” meaning one made pleasing (69:21).
rows.anchor: مدفوق أي مصبوب في الرحم، وهو المني، فاعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular water refers to both male and female fluids, since the child is formed from both and they mix together.
rows.anchor: وأراد ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، لأن الولد مخلوق منهما، وجعله واحدا لامتزاجهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is located between the man's backbone and the woman's breastbones.
rows.anchor: يعني صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarāʾib is the plural of tarība and refers to the bones of the chest and neck.
rows.anchor: و"الترائب" جمع التربية، وهي عظام الصدر والنحر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the tarāʾib as the place where a necklace lies on the chest.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي موضع القلادة من الصدر.

rows.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wālibī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the location is between a woman's breasts.
rows.anchor: وروى الوالبي عنه: بين ثديي المرأة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the location as the upper chest or throat area.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: النحر. وقال ابن زيد: الصدر.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the location as the chest.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: النحر. وقال ابن زيد: الصدر.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the return is restoring the semen to the urethra.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: على رد النطفة في الإحليل.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says it is restoring the fluid to the loins from which it came.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: على رد الماء في الصلب الذي خرج منه.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God can return the human being to fluid as he was before.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان من قبل لقادر.

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says God can return a person from old age to youth, youth to childhood, and childhood to semen.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: [إن شاء رده] (2) من الكبر إلى الشباب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God can withhold the fluid so that it does not emerge.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنه على حبس ذلك الماء لقادر حتى لا يخرج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the return as resurrection; Baghawī prefers this view because the following verse refers to Judgment Day and the testing of hidden deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن الله تعالى على بعث الإنسان وإعادته قادر وهذا أولى الأقاويل لقوله: {يوم تبلى السرائر}

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil say that the hidden deeds are tested on that day.
rows.anchor: تظهر الخفايا قال قتادة ومقاتل: تختبر [الأعمال] (3)

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says the hidden matters are obligatory acts such as fasting, prayer, ablution, and ritual washing, known between God and a servant; they are tested to reveal who performed or neglected them.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح: السرائر فرائض الأعمال، كالصوم والصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says every secret is in God's hand on Judgment Day, becoming adornment on some faces and disgrace on others: the obedient shine, while the negligent are dusty-faced.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر: بيدي الله عز وجل يوم القيامة كل سر، فيكون زينا في وجوه وشينا في وجوه،

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of resurrection has no strength to protect himself from God's punishment and no helper against God.
rows.anchor: ما لهذا الإنسان المنكر للبعث من قوة يمتنع بها من عذاب الله ولا ناصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's recurring return is rain, which comes back year after year.
rows.anchor: أي ذات المطر لأنه يرجع كل عام ويتكرر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the returning thing as clouds that bring back rain.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو السحاب يرجع بالمطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth splits open for plants, trees, and rivers to emerge.
rows.anchor: تتصدع وتنشق عن النبات والأشجار والأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer refers to the Qur'an, a true, decisive word that separates truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: قوله: {إنه} يعني القرآن {لقول فصل} حق وجد يفصل بين الحق والباطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is neither play nor falsehood.
rows.anchor: باللعب والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists fear the Prophet while outwardly presenting themselves as the opposite of what they are.
rows.anchor: يخافون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويظهرون ما هم على خلافه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet promises that one who masters the Qur'an and acts by it will have parents crowned on Judgment Day with light brighter than the sun in a worldly house; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " من قرأ القرآن فأحكمه وعمل بما فيه

words: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: When ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn sees a man reciting Qur'an to people and asking them for money, he says the verse's return formula and recalls the Prophet's warning to ask God through Qur'an, since some will recite it to solicit from people.
rows.anchor: عن رجل أن عمران بن حصين مر على رجل يقرأ على قوم فلما قرأ سأل فقال عمران: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī notes al-Tirmidhī's version traces the report through al-Ḥasan from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and al-Bukhārī clarifies this is Khaythama al-Baṣrī, not Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسماعيل هو خيثمة البصري الذي روى عنه جابر الجعفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Muḥammad with guidance and the true religion as mercy to all, glad tidings for believers, and warning for opponents; through him prophethood was completed, the message sealed, and noble character perfected.
rows.anchor: أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق رحمة للعالمين، وبشيرا للمؤمنين، ونذيرا للمخالفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's Qur'an is a light that guides people away from error and saves them from ignorance.
rows.anchor: وأنزل عليه بفضله نورا هدى به من الضلالة، وأنقذ به من الجهالة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow the Qur'an attain success, while those who turn away after hearing it incur loss.
rows.anchor: وحكم بالفلاح لمن تبعه، وبالخسارة لمن أعرض عنه بعد ما سمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is inimitable: creation cannot answer it or produce a sura like it, although God makes its recitation easy for people.
rows.anchor: أعجز الخليقة عن معارضته وعن الإتيان بسورة من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an commands and forbids, gives glad tidings and warnings, offers admonitions, recounts past peoples for reflection, presents parables, and points to signs of divine oneness for contemplation.
rows.anchor: أمر فيه وزجر، وبشر وأنذر وذكر المواعظ ليتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Realizing these purposes requires knowledge of tafsīr and its features, occasions of revelation, rulings, abrogating and abrogated verses, and specific and general language.
rows.anchor: ولا حصول لهذه المقاصد فيه إلا بدراية تفسيره وأعلامه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is an inimitable, deep sea whose scholarly secrets and true meanings have no end.
rows.anchor: ثم هو كلام معجز وبحر عميق، لا نهاية لأسرار علومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early scholars wrote books on Qur'anic sciences according to their understanding and knowledge; Baghawī thanks God for their efforts and asks mercy for them all.
rows.anchor: وقد ألف أئمة السلف في أنواع علومه كتبا، كل على قدر فهمه، ومبلغ علمه،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that fire would not touch a Qur'an contained in a hide; an anonymous gloss explains this as meaning that a person who carries and recites the Qur'an will not be touched by Hellfire on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت عقبة بن عامر يقول: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An anonymous gloss says that whoever carries and recites the Qur'an will not be touched by the Fire on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه من حمل القرآن وقرأه لم تمسه النار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls the Qur'an God's banquet, rope, clear light, healing, protection, and salvation; it does not mislead or warp, its wonders never end or wear out through repetition, and each letter recited earns ten good deeds, with alif, lām, and mīm counted separately.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: " [إن هذا القرآن مأدبة الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Baghawī notes that some transmit Ibn Masʿūd's Qur'an report as a Prophetic report; he also gives a separate chain in which the Prophet states its meaning.
rows.anchor: ورواه بعضهم عن ابن مسعود مرفوعا

rows.speaker: أبو الطفيل
rows.claim: ʿUmar approves appointing the freedman Ibn Abzā over Mecca because he recites Qur'an, knows inheritance law, and judges; he invokes the Prophet's statement that God raises people through the Qur'an, though the excerpt ends mid-report.
rows.anchor: عن عامر بن واثلة أبي الطفيل " أن نافع بن عبد الحارث لقي عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says the proficient Qur'an reciter is among the noble, righteous scribes, while one who struggles reciting receives two rewards; Baghawī grades it ṣaḥīḥ and gives a wording variant from Hishām al-Dastawāʾī.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " مثل الماهر بالقرآن مثل السفرة الكرام البررة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the believer who recites Qur'an to a citron, the believer who does not recite to a date, the wicked reciter to a fragrant but tasteless herb, and the wicked non-reciter to a bitter colocynth; Baghawī calls it ṣaḥīḥ and notes al-Bukhārī's transmission.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: " مثل المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells the Qur'an's companion to recite, ascend, and recite as in worldly life; the person's station is at the last verse recited. Al-Tirmidhī calls the report ṣaḥīḥ ḥasan.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يقال لصاحب القرآن اقرأ: وارتق ورتل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says Qur'an will intercede for its companions; al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān will appear like clouds, canopies, or flocks of birds arguing for their reader, and al-Baqara's recitation is blessing while abandoning it is regret and sorcerers cannot withstand it. Baghawī grades it ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أنه حدثه قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " اقرؤوا القرآن فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شافعا لأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explaining a verse's occasion, circumstances, and story is permissible only through verified transmitted reports and hearing.
rows.anchor: أما التفسير: وهو الكلام في أسباب نزول الآية وشأنها وقصتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr derives from tafsira, the water sample a physician examines to uncover a patient's illness; a commentator similarly uncovers a verse's circumstances and story.
rows.anchor: وأصل التفسير من التفسرة وهي: الدليل من الماء الذي ينظر فيه الطبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl derives from awwal, return: to make something return or turn it so that it returns.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق التأويل من الأول وهو الرجوع. يقال: أولته فآل أي: صرفته فانصرف.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the Qur'an came in seven aḥruf, and every verse has an outer and inner aspect, a limit, and a point of ascent; another wording gives every letter a limit and every limit an ascent. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف، لكل آية منها ظهر وبطن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation takes the outer aspect as Qur'anic wording and the inner aspect as its interpretation.
rows.anchor: قيل: الظهر لفظ القرآن والبطن تأويله.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the outer aspect reports how earlier peoples disobeyed and were punished, while its inner lesson warns readers not to repeat their acts and suffer the same fate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الظهر ما حدث عن أقوام أنهم عصوا فعوقبوا فهو في الظاهر خبر وباطنه عظة وتحذير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view interprets outer and inner as recitation and understanding: recitation is reading as revealed, while the inner aspect is reflection and contemplation, linked to 73:4 and 38:29.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى الظهر والبطن: التلاوة والتفهم، يقول: لكل آية ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation is gained through learning and memorization by study; understanding is gained through sincere intention, reverence, and a sound inward disposition.
rows.anchor: ثم التلاوة تكون بالتعلم والحفظ بالدرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every letter has a boundary in recitation and interpretation: recitation must not go beyond the written Qur'an, and interpretation must not exceed what has been transmitted.
rows.anchor: ففي التلاوة لا يجاوز المصحف، وفي التفسير لا يجاوز المسموع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maṭlaʿ is an ascent toward knowledge of a subject, and can mean understanding; God may open interpretive meanings to contemplative readers that others do not receive.
rows.anchor: وقد يفتح الله على المدبر والمتفكر في التأويل والمعاني ما لا يفتح على غيره،

none: The segment lists chains for named tafsir transmissions but gives no exegetical claims or report content.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Burayda reports the Prophet saying al-Baqara's recitation is blessing, abandoning it regret, and magicians cannot withstand it; al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān shade their companion, while Qur'an rewards the devoted reader and parents and raises the reader through Paradise. Baghawī grades this report gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال كنت جالسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسمعته يقول: " اقرءوا سورة البقرة فإن أخذها بركة وتركها حسرة ولا يستطيعها البطلة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever listens to a Qur'anic verse receives a multiplied good deed, and whoever recites a verse will have a light on Judgment Day; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من استمع إلى آية من كتاب الله عز وجل كتبت له حسنة مضاعفة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says three verses recited in prayer are better than three large pregnant camels returned to their owner; Baghawī grades the report ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أيحب أحدكم إذا رجع إلى أهله أن يجد فيه ثلاث خلفات
